distinguishing_features: Detects subsurface shear micro-crack nucleation via transient Rayleigh-wave acoustic-emission bursts, instead of the closest art's speed-corrected mesh-stiffness phase modulation of a rotating gear pair.
Uses a distributed rail-mounted sensor array with ~300 mm spacing derived from the Rayleigh wavelength (~57 mm at 50 kHz) to cover the curve gauge corner.

Raises a real-time alarm from an event-rate threshold (>=3 bursts/minute at 5 dB above baseline) rather than periodic manual ultrasonic inspection or envelope demodulation against a shaft-angle reference.
Targets rail rolling-contact fatigue (shelling precursors) at curve gauge corners using the already-installed rail sensors and existing data-acquisition channel.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to detect, in real time and before visible surface damage, the early nucleation of rolling-contact-fatigue micro-cracks (shelling precursors) in rails at curve gauge corners, using surface-mounted sensors and the existing data-acquisition infrastructure.
parsed.viable_reason: Rayleigh-wave acoustic-emission detection of crack-nucleation bursts in rail steel is physically sound (the calculated shear- and Rayleigh-wave speeds are correct in magnitude) and the 30-day event-rate trial with a defined kill criterion is executable with the stated sensors and data-acquisition system.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior Art 1 already teaches acoustic-emission/vibration condition monitoring as the standard approach for early fatigue-crack detection, so deploying burst-type AE event detection on rails with wavelength-based spacing and a baseline-plus-dB threshold is a routine domain transfer with routine parameter choices, not a non-obvious mechanism departure.
